```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
```

# Overview

This report reads a fitted MOFA results object and generates diagnostic and exploratory plots using `MOFA2`. The workflow assumes that MOFA analysis has already been performed and that the fitted model is stored in the file specified by `params$mofa_res_fname`.

Additional plotting options are available in the MOFA2 reference manual and tutorials.

# Load packages

```{r load-packages}
library(MOFA2)
library(ggplot2)
library(corrplot)
```

# Report parameters

The main user-adjustable parameters are defined in the YAML header at the top of this `.Rmd` file. They can also be overridden when calling `rmarkdown::render()`.

```{r show-parameters}
params
```

# Load MOFA model

```{r load-model}
mofa_res_fname <- params$mofa_res_fname

if (!file.exists(mofa_res_fname)) {
  stop("The MOFA results file does not exist: ", mofa_res_fname)
}

model <- load_model(mofa_res_fname)
```

# Model options and quality control

The following output records the model options used during fitting, which can serve as a useful reminder when reviewing the report.

```{r model-options}
model@model_options
```

The data and training options are not printed by default, but the commands below can be uncommented if needed.

```{r data-training-options, eval=FALSE}
model@data_options
model@training_options
```

The quality-control summary reports data views and warning messages generated during MOFA execution.

```{r quality-control}
MOFA2:::.quality_control(model)
```

# Data overview

This plot shows what data views are available for which samples.

```{r data-overview, fig.height=6}
plot_data_overview(model)
```

# Variance explained

The table below reports the variance explained by each factor, followed by a plot of variance explained by view and factor.

```{r variance-explained-table}
calculate_variance_explained(model)
```

```{r variance-explained-plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=7}
plot_variance_explained(model, x = "view", y = "factor")
```

# Correlation between factors

MOFA factors are generally expected to be approximately pairwise orthogonal. If groups were used in the MOFA run, the `groups` argument can be adjusted to specify the group or groups whose samples should be used for computing correlations.

```{r factor-correlation, fig.width=9, fig.height=9}
factor_values <- Reduce(rbind, get_factors(model, groups = "all", factors = "all"))
corrplot(cor(factor_values))
```

# Association between factors and clinical covariates

The covariates tested here are controlled by `params$col_names_to_use`.

`correlate_factors_with_covariates()` computes the Pearson correlation between each factor and each covariate and uses a t-test to assign a p-value to that correlation. For categorical covariates, MOFA2 converts covariates to factor levels, so the p-values are most interpretable for binary categorical covariates.

```{r factor-covariate-logp, fig.width=11, fig.height=8}
col_names_to_use <- params$col_names_to_use

correlate_factors_with_covariates(
  model,
  col_names_to_use,
  plot = "log_pval",
  display_numbers = TRUE
)
```

```{r factor-covariate-r, fig.width=11, fig.height=8}
correlate_factors_with_covariates(
  model,
  col_names_to_use,
  plot = "r"
)
```

# Selected factor plots

The selected factors are controlled by `params$sel_facs`, and the metadata column used for coloring is controlled by `params$metadata_col`.

```{r selected-factor-settings}
sel_facs <- params$sel_facs
metadata_col <- params$metadata_col

sel_facs
metadata_col
```

## Factor values across samples

```{r plot-factor, fig.width=10, fig.height=7}
plot_factor(model, factor = sel_facs, color_by = metadata_col)
```

## Factor values with violin plots

```{r plot-factor-violin, fig.width=10, fig.height=7}
plot_factor(
  model,
  factor = sel_facs,
  color_by = metadata_col,
  add_violin = TRUE,
  dodge = TRUE
)
```

## Pairwise factor plots

```{r pairwise-factor-plots, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
plot_factors(
  model,
  factor = sel_facs,
  color_by = metadata_col,
  color_name = metadata_col
)
```

# Top feature weights

These plots show features with the largest weights for a selected factor and view. This can help identify features that are strongly associated with the selected factor.

```{r top-weight-settings}
top_weight_factor <- params$top_weight_factor
top_weight_nfeatures <- params$top_weight_nfeatures
top_weight_views <- params$top_weight_views

top_weight_factor
top_weight_nfeatures
top_weight_views
```

```{r top-weights, fig.width=11, fig.height=8, results='asis'}
for (view_i in top_weight_views) {
  cat("\n\n## Top weights: ", view_i, "\n\n", sep = "")
  print(
    plot_top_weights(
      model,
      view = view_i,
      factor = top_weight_factor,
      nfeatures = top_weight_nfeatures
    )
  )
}
```

# Dimensionality reduction

The following section uses the learned factor values to run t-SNE and UMAP on the sample space, then colors samples by the selected metadata column. The embedding methods are stochastic, so results may vary across runs unless the relevant underlying functions control the random seed.

```{r run-dimensionality-reduction, eval=params$run_dimred}
model <- run_tsne(model)
model <- run_umap(model)
```

```{r plot-tsne, fig.width=9, fig.height=7, eval=params$run_dimred}
plot_dimred(model, method = "TSNE", color_by = metadata_col)
```

```{r plot-umap, fig.width=9, fig.height=7, eval=params$run_dimred}
plot_dimred(model, method = "UMAP", color_by = metadata_col)
```

# Data heatmaps

These heatmaps cluster a view using the features with the highest absolute weights for a selected factor. Clustering is performed using the measurements in the view data matrix on which MOFA was trained. The sample annotations are controlled by `params$heatmap_annotation_samples`.

```{r heatmap-settings}
heatmap_factor <- params$heatmap_factor
heatmap_features <- params$heatmap_features
heatmap_views <- params$heatmap_views
heatmap_annotation_samples <- params$heatmap_annotation_samples

heatmap_factor
heatmap_features
heatmap_views
heatmap_annotation_samples
```

```{r data-heatmaps, fig.width=11, fig.height=9, results='asis'}
for (view_i in heatmap_views) {
  cat("\n\n## Heatmap: ", view_i, "\n\n", sep = "")
  print(
    plot_data_heatmap(
      model,
      factor = heatmap_factor,
      view = view_i,
      features = heatmap_features,
      annotation_samples = heatmap_annotation_samples
    )
  )
}
```
